newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht firmer in quiet post-G7 trade.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht firmer in quiet post-G7 trade.

text.p: * Thai baht firmer, but still on upper end of mid-rate as dollar comes off highs against majors after weekend G7 meeting.
* Indonesian, Malaysian and Singapore foreign exchange markets closed for Moslem New Year.
The Thai baht firmed in slow Monday trade as the dollar came off its highs against the mark and yen after a weekend Group of Seven meeting signalled a strong desire for currency stability.
Dealers in Bangkok said the absence of Singapore players dampened trading interest in the baht.
The baht was quoted at 25.920-25.940 to the dollar at 0425 GMT against 25.990-26.040 late on Friday. The Bank of Thailand set the midrate at 25.90 on Monday.
"It's trading on the upper side of the midrate but the market seems quiet today with the holiday in Singapore," said a deaker at Bangkok Bank.
Media and market speculation that international heavyweight George Soros was preparing to attack the baht was having little impact on Monday morning, dealers said.
"There have been a lot of rumours in the last two weeks. In the end it comes down to who you believe," said a dealer at Thai Danu Bank.
"I think the market has relaxed this morning. I think it will be fairly steady for a couple of days," he said.

The overnight interbank rate eased to 24-25 percent early, from 25-26 percent late on Friday as liquidity increased following the passing of bank reserve requirements and the end of Lunar New Year festival demand, dealers said.
-- James Mclean in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
